issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Review: the AI's proposed plan changes NEVER render (approve/modify flow is dead), the Insights tab is always empty, and the protein target always shows "/ 0g" — all rooted in the /reviews serializer. Real users can never see or approve the coach's weekly plan adjustments.

Root cause (backend app/routes/reviews.py::_serialize_review + frontend src/services/review.service.ts::normalizeReview).

1) PROPOSED CHANGES (HIGH — core feature dead): db_models.py:1734 declares `proposed_changes = db.Column(JSON)`, but the engine writes it as a STRING via `review.proposed_changes = json.dumps(proposed_changes)` (app/services/weekly_review.py:534) and reads it back with `json.loads(review.proposed_changes)` everywhere (weekly_review.py:653/857, scheduler_jobs.py:627) — proving the attribute is a JSON string. `_serialize_review` (reviews.py:57) returns `r.proposed_changes` WITHOUT json.loads, so the API sends proposed_changes as a JSON string e.g. "[{...}]". FE normalizeReview (review.service.ts:46) only handles an Array or an {adjustments:[...]} object: Array.isArray(string) is false and string.adjustments is undefined -> `?? []`. proposed_changes collapses to []. PlanDiffViewer shows "No plan changes proposed this week" and the primary CTA is disabled ("Select changes to approve"); the user can only Keep Current / Discuss. Secondary: even if the string were parsed, the engine's per-change shape is {category, current_value, proposed_value, reason} — no id/label and different key names than the FE's {id, field, label, current, proposed} — so cards would render blank and selection (keyed on change.id) would break; the {adjustments:{type,from,to,target}} branch matches a shape the engine never emits. Masked in QA only because dev ?demo=1 (WeeklyReviewScreen.tsx:241-322) injects a proper array.

2) INSIGHTS (MED): _serialize_review emits NO top-level `insights` field (getById returns none; /latest only nests them under data.adjustment.insights, which the FE never reads). FE `insights: raw.insights ?? []` (review.service.ts:51) -> always []. The AI Insights section reads "No notable patterns this week." on every real review.

3) PROTEIN TARGET (MED): the model has target_daily_protein (set weekly_review.py:516) but _serialize_review omits it (and target_daily_steps). FE `protein_target: raw.target_daily_protein ?? 0` (review.service.ts:56) -> 0. The Overview chip renders "{avg_protein}g / 0g" on every real review (calorie target + meals serialize fine; protein target uniquely does not).

Repro: open /weekly-review for a user with a real generated review (NOT ?demo=1). Overview shows "Ng / 0g" protein; Insights tab shows "No notable patterns this week"; Plan Changes shows "No plan changes proposed" with the approve CTA disabled — even though the AI generated proposed changes + insights.

Expected: proposed changes render as selectable diff cards with a working Approve / Approve-N-of-M; Insights shows the week's detected patterns; protein target shows the real value (e.g. "158g / 160g").

Fix (all in _serialize_review, one place): json.loads(proposed_changes) before returning and normalize each item to {id, field/category, label, current, proposed, reason} (OR relax normalizeReview to JSON.parse a string + map the engine's current_value/proposed_value keys); add a top-level `insights`; add target_daily_protein + target_daily_steps. Re-QA the approve/modify/reject round-trip after the fix.

It also omitted a top-level insights field and target_daily_protein/steps, so Insights always read No notable patterns and protein showed slash 0g. [bug-hunt] Ad-hoc "Log activity": removing ONE logged activity silently deletes EVERY same-named activity that day (data loss). The new sheet's Remove (X) and the plan tick-off both delete by name+date, but log always inserts a new row.

Root cause (frontend + backend):
- Remove passes the NAME, not the row id: src/components/activity/LogActivitySheet.tsx:327 -> removeMut.mutate(entry.activity_name) -> loggingService.unlogActivity({activity_name, log_date}) (logging.service.ts:104).
- Backend DELETE /api/logs/activity deletes ALL rows matching user+date+lower(name): app/routes/logging.py:1228-1230 (.delete(synchronize_session=False), no id, no LIMIT 1). Returns {deleted: N}.
- POST always INSERTs a fresh row (logging.py:1191-1202, no upsert/dedup). No unique constraint on (name,date) — db_models.py ActivityLog has only a NON-unique idx_activity_log_user_date. So two same-name rows/day are allowed and each renders as its own <li key={entry.id}> (LogActivitySheet.tsx:303).
- Same by-name delete is used by the plan tick-off: src/components/activity/ActivityMarkSection.tsx:101 unlogActivityMut.mutate({activity_name: activity.name, log_date}).

Repro (single feature):
1. /activity -> Log activity -> type Cardio, Name "Run", Duration 30 -> Save.
2. Log activity again -> Name "Run", Duration 20 -> Save.
3. Reopen the sheet: both "Run" entries show under "Also logged today".

Expected: only that one entry is removed.

[bug-hunt] Profile > "Adjust macro targets" is a silent no-op for users who HAVE a plan (the default onboarding outcome), yet shows a success toast ("Your daily calorie and macro goals now apply across the app").

ROOT CAUSE (traced both repos): the editor (ProfileMacroTargetsCard -> PUT /profile/macro-targets) writes ONLY UserProfile.target_{protein,carbs,fats}_grams + UserHealthProfile.target_kcal (backend app/routes/profile.py:546-553). But the /nutrition ring reads dietPlan.macros_target (src/pages/_components/nutrition/useNutritionData.tsx:363), and GET /diet/plan PREFERS the active plan WeeklyMacroTarget rows and only falls back to the UserProfile columns when there is NO active plan (backend.py:6686-6712, "prefer WeeklyMacroTarget (calculated), fallback to profile"). Onboarding always builds a plan and seeds WeeklyMacroTarget (plan_generator.py:3237/3379, plans.py:808), so real users hit the WeeklyMacroTarget branch and the edited columns are never read -> editing macro targets changes nothing on the ring / per-meal splits.

SECONDARY (same feature): even for no-plan users the /nutrition CALORIE target is Atwater-derived from the macro grams (useNutritionData.tsx:387-393: protein*4+carbs*4+fats*9), so the "Daily calories" field (target_kcal) is never consumed by the ring -- the reconciliation banner presents calories & macros as two independent knobs but the ring only ever uses macros. Coach-wizard context recomputes target_kcal from scratch (backend.py:11287 _calc[calorie_target]) rather than reading the saved column, so it does not rescale either.

EXPECTED: after Save the nutrition ring + per-meal splits reflect the new targets for ALL users (the toast promise). ACTUAL: no change for plan users (the majority); the calorie field never affects the ring even for no-plan users.

REPRO: onboard so an active plan exists -> Profile -> Adjust macro targets -> change Protein/Carbs/Fat + Daily calories -> Save (success toast) -> open /nutrition -> macro/calorie target rings unchanged.

FIX options: (a) editor also writes the active plan current-week WeeklyMacroTarget row (protein_g/carbs_g/fat_g + calories) so plan-derived targets change; (b) GET /diet/plan prefer a user manual override when present; (c) at minimum stop claiming "applies across the app" for plan users.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner-group activity events show the wrong relative time and sort out of order in the partner chat thread, because the /events endpoint serializes their UTC timestamp WITHOUT a Z suffix while every sibling timestamp in the same thread DOES append Z.

ROOT CAUSE (offset-less UTC — same class as the already-fixed social-feed + coach-social cases, but a distinct THIRD endpoint):
- Backend: app/routes/partner_groups.py:1250 (GET /partner-groups/<group_id>/events) returns 'created_at': r.created_at.isoformat() with NO Z. PartnerGroupEvent.created_at is a naive UTC column (db_models.py:2286, default=datetime.utcnow). The codebase convention is .isoformat() + "Z" (admin_v2/ai_dashboard.py, coach.py:85, and the partner-group MESSAGE serializer backend.py:5617/5679/5748 all append Z).
- Frontend: SessionStartedCard.tsx:29 and MealLoggedCard.tsx:28 compute relativeTime = Date.now() - new Date(iso).getTime(). An offset-less ISO string is parsed as LOCAL time, so for the primary market (IST, +5:30) a just-created event is read ~5.5h in the past. PartnerChatThread.tsx:292 also uses timestampOf(e.created_at) as the interleave sortKey, while chat messages use sent_at (which IS Z-suffixed / true UTC).

EXPECTED: an event that just happened shows "just now"; events and messages interleave in true chronological order.
ACTUAL (IST viewer): a just-happened "Mike started Push A" / meal-logged card shows "5h" ago; and because same-moment messages carry a Z (real UTC epoch) while events are shifted -5.5h, events sort ~5.5h earlier than messages that actually happened at the same time, so events cluster wrongly early in the thread. US/negative-offset viewers hit the mirror case: relativeTime clamps with Math.max(0,...) so everything reads "just now".

REPRO: open /partners/:groupId as an IST-timezone user; have a group member start a session or log a meal; observe the event card timestamp ("5h" instead of "just now") and its position relative to same-time chat messages.

FIX: append Z in partner_groups.py:1250 (r.created_at.isoformat() + "Z") to match the message serializers — one line, mirrors the b3f0/c1a7 fixes. (partner_groups.py:1393 reaction created_at is offset-less too but renders no relative time; optional for consistency.)
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: the GET /partner-groups/<id>/events endpoint serialized each event's UTC created_at with .isoformat() but WITHOUT a 'Z' suffix, while every sibling timestamp in the thread (chat messages) does append Z. The app parsed the offset-less string as LOCAL time, so for IST users a just-created event card showed '5h' ago instead of 'just now' and sorted ~5.5h out of order against messages. Fix: append '+Z' to the events serializer (and the DM-reaction serializer) so both are true UTC, matching the message serializers. Capture shows the thread now rendering a just-logged meal as 'just now' and a 6-min-old session as '6m', in correct order.

judge.note: Root-caused + one-line fix mirroring the two prior offset-less-UTC fixes; backend regression test asserts Z-suffix (32/32 green); scenario capture confirms FE renders correct relative time + order; deployed live to prod.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Goal ETA on the Log-Weight "Goal Progress" card projects the goal date from an EWMA-SMOOTHED weekly rate but divides it into an UNSMOOTHED remaining distance, and reads trend direction from a single raw weigh-in — so the projected date is wrong by the daily water-weight swing on ~every view, and can invert outright.

ROOT CAUSE (src/pages/LogWeight.tsx:394-404 + src/lib/goal-eta.ts): computeGoalEta gets ratePerWeekKg = weightTrend.ratePerWeek (EWMA alpha=0.25, whose entire purpose is to cancel the 0.5-1.5 kg daily water/sodium noise), but remainingKg = goalProgress.remaining and direction = goalProgress.direction — both derived from goalProgress.currentKg = last_log.weight_kg, the RAW latest reading (seeded into the input at line 94, used at rest at lines 318/337/340-341). Smoothed rate + unsmoothed distance = apples-to-oranges.

MANIFESTATION 1 (distance error, ~every view): goal 75 kg, EWMA trend 76.2 kg descending -0.35 kg/wk -> true remaining 1.2 kg -> ~3 wk. If today's raw last_log came in at 77.5 kg (normal high-water morning) -> remaining = |77.5-75| = 2.5 -> weeks = round(2.5/0.35) = 7 -> "On track for <date> - ~7 wk". Projected date off by ~4 weeks from one noisy reading, and it jerks daily with water weight — defeating the EWMA the rate half already applies.

MANIFESTATION 2 (direction inversion): goal 75, EWMA trend 76.2 still descending -0.35 kg/wk, but the latest saved reading dipped to 74.0 kg (dehydrated morning; below goal though the trend is clearly above). goalProgress.direction = currentKg(74.0) < goalKg(75) -> "gain"; computeGoalEta towardGoal for "gain" needs rate>0 but rate is -0.35 -> off_track -> card shows "Not trending toward your goal yet - Keep logging to project your goal date." while the Goal Progress bar directly above reads ~99% and the trend caption shows the user steadily losing toward goal. Opposite of reality.

EXPECTED: the ETA remaining distance AND direction should be measured from the SAME EWMA-smoothed weight the rate comes from (weightTrend.kg) — remaining = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg|, direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg — so a single noisy weigh-in cannot swing or invert the projection.

REPRO: /log-weight with >=3 logged points and a live goal; have the most recent saved weigh-in deviate from the smoothed trend by ~1-2.5 kg (routine daily fluctuation). The "~N wk / On track for <date>" shifts by weeks vs the trend-implied ETA; when the raw reading crosses the goal line the card flips to "keep logging". tsc + the pure goal-eta.ts unit tests pass — the defect is the input wiring in LogWeight.tsx, not the helper.

FIX: pass remainingKg = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg| and derive direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg (the EWMA trend), instead of goalProgress (raw last_log / live input).
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: LogWeight.tsx fed computeGoalEta a smoothed EWMA rate but an UNSMOOTHED remaining distance + direction (goalProgress.remaining/direction, both from the raw last_log weight) - so one noisy weigh-in swung the projected date by weeks and could invert direction to a false 'keep logging'. Fix: remaining = |weightTrend.kg - goalKg| and direction from weightTrend.kg vs goalKg (same EWMA weight the rate uses). Proof: raw last_log dipped to 74.0 kg below the 75 kg goal while EWMA trend ~76 kg descending - pre-fix inverted to 'keep logging'; post-fix reads 'On track for Jul 19, 2026'. tsc clean, goal-eta unit 8/8.

judge.note: Exact root-cause fix (matches the bug report's prescribed wiring change); surgical 12-line edit in LogWeight.tsx; full-screen 390x844 proof on the correct /log-weight screen shows the manifestation-2 inversion gone (raw 74.0 dip below goal now correctly reads 'On track for Jul 19, 2026' from the EWMA trend instead of 'keep logging'); tsc clean, goal-eta unit 8/8 green. Only caveat: proof uses a route.fulfill scenario mock since all onboarded accounts were deleted in the prelaunch cleanup - the mock faithfully drives the exact code path.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] In the Recipe Detail meal editor (/recipe-detail, reached by tapping a meal in Nutrition or MealDetail), editing or removing an individual part of a COMBINED ingredient row (an ingredient whose NAME joins foods, e.g. "Dal with Rice" / "Chicken and Vegetables" / "Rice + Beans") does not persist. Save shows a "Recipe updated for today" success toast, but on reload the removed part reappears and any uneven per-part quantities are silently redistributed EVENLY.

ROOT CAUSE (frontend expand/collapse vs backend re-split mismatch):
- GET /diet/recipes/<id> expands a combined-name ingredient into per-part rows with STRING ids like "42-0","42-1" via _expand_combined (backend.py:6971-7090); per_part_qty = round(parent_qty / part_count). So one DB Ingredient (id 42 "Dal with Rice", 200g) is served to the FE as two editable rows: "Dal" ("42-0", 100g) + "Rice" ("42-1", 100g).
- RecipeDetail renders each split row as a normal editable/removable row with no split awareness (RecipeDetail.tsx:420-524) — the user naturally edits/removes them individually.
- handleSaveChanges (RecipeDetail.tsx:146-177) COLLAPSES every split row back to its parent INTEGER id and SUMS the quantities: rawId.includes('-') ? parseInt(rawId.split('-')[0]) — so both "42-0" and "42-1" fold into ingredient_id 42 with quantity = sum. The per-part distribution is discarded; a removed part just lowers the parent sum.
- POST /diet/log-modification is a full-replace UserMealModification keyed by integer ingredient_id (backend.py:7418-7420).
- The next GET reads the modification back and re-expands it by NAME through the SAME _expand_combined (backend.py:7110-7126) — the parent name still contains both foods, so it re-splits EVENLY again.

MANIFESTATION A (remove doesn't stick): remove "Rice" from "Dal with Rice", Save. currentIngredients now has only "Dal" (100g) -> payload {ingredient_id:42, quantity:100}. Reload -> _expand_combined("Dal with Rice", 100) -> "Dal" 50g + "Rice" 50g. Rice is BACK (at half) and Dal was halved. The removal is silently undone.

MANIFESTATION B (uneven edit redistributed): set "Dal" 150g, leave "Rice" 100g, Save. Payload {42, 250}. Reload -> 250/2 -> "Dal" 125g + "Rice" 125g. The "more dal, less rice" intent is erased.

Only affects ingredients whose NAME combines foods (split on " with "/" and "/&/+), which is common in this India-focused app's AI meal plans (dal-and-rice, paneer-with-roti, chana-and-rice). Single-name ingredients round-trip fine (len(parts)<2 -> same integer id in and out).

EXPECTED: removing a part removes it; an uneven per-part edit persists as edited.
ACTUAL: success toast, then reload reverts the removal and evens out the quantities (silent data loss).

REPRO: Nutrition -> tap a meal whose recipe has a combined-name ingredient -> in the ingredient list remove one half of that row (or bump only one half) -> Save -> reopen the recipe: the removed half is back and both halves are equal.

FIX: preserve the expanded view across the round-trip — e.g. have the backend NOT re-split when an active modification exists (persist + read the expanded rows keyed by the string part id), or have the FE send per-part quantities the backend can honor, so a removed/resized part is not reconstituted from the parent name.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + shipped (FE fc5eedf2, backend 2efde98 deployed to prod, health OK). Root cause: GET /diet/recipes/<id> re-expanded stored modifications by the parent combined NAME, so removing/uneven-editing one part of a 'Dal with Rice' row was reverted to an even 50/50 split on reload. Fix: save now persists the exact edited display rows (schema rows_v2) and the backend returns them verbatim (no re-split); legacy portion-scaler payloads unchanged. Verified by 2 new RecipeDetail page tests (per-part removal + uneven qty persist without collapsing to the parent) — full suite 29/29 green. Flagging for review because the live /recipe-detail round-trip can't be screenshotted headlessly: the QA test account is data-less (empty /nutrition, no meal recipe to open). Please verify on-device, or it rides the next alpha build.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] On the Recipe Detail meal editor (/recipe-detail), any Save silently DELETES "unmatched" ingredient rows from today's recipe — even when the user only meant to tweak a different ingredient — while still showing a "Recipe updated for today" success toast.

ROOT CAUSE:
- The backend serves ingredient rows it could not resolve to a food-DB entry with id=null + _unmatched:true (backend.py:7081-7089, the _expand_combined public-DB-miss + no-serving-size fallback). RecipeDetail renders these identically to normal rows — full stepper + qty input + remove button (RecipeDetail.tsx:420-524). The "prompt the user to set a quantity" comment at RecipeDetail.tsx:76-79 is NOT actually implemented; an unmatched row just looks like any other editable ingredient (it only lacks the "N cal" subline because it has no resolved macros).
- handleSaveChanges (RecipeDetail.tsx:146-177) builds the save payload by iterating currentIngredients with `if (ing.id == null) continue;` (line ~152) — so EVERY unmatched row (id=null) is skipped from the modifications payload.
- POST /diet/log-modification is a full REPLACE (backend.py:7418-7420) and the next GET rebuilds the ingredient list SOLELY from the saved modification's ingredients (backend.py:7110-7126). Because the unmatched rows were never sent, they are absent from the modification and vanish from the recipe on reload.

So: open a recipe that contains ANY unmatched ingredient, tweak an unrelated MATCHED ingredient's quantity, tap Save -> success toast -> reopen -> the unmatched ingredient(s) are gone. The user never asked to remove them and got no warning. (Distinct from i-20260713-c3f1: that is the combined-row re-split revert; this is the id==null skip on save.)

EXPECTED: Save preserves ingredients the user did not remove (or at minimum warns that unmatched items can't be saved).
ACTUAL: unmatched rows are silently dropped on the first Save of any change; false success toast.

REPRO: open a recipe whose ingredient list shows a row with no "N cal" subline (an unmatched row) alongside normal rows -> change any OTHER ingredient's quantity -> Save -> reopen the recipe: the macro-less row is gone.

FIX: don't skip id==null rows on save — carry unmatched rows through the modification (e.g. by name/index so the backend can re-attach them), or block/flag the save with a clear message instead of silently dropping them; align with the render comment that promises the user can set their quantity.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + shipped (FE fc5eedf2, backend 2efde98 deployed to prod, health OK). Root cause: unmatched ingredient rows (id==null, no resolved macros) were skipped from the save payload ('if (ing.id == null) continue'), so the full-replace modification dropped them on reload while still showing a success toast. Fix: save now sends every displayed row verbatim by name (schema rows_v2, unmatched flag preserved) and the backend returns them as-is. Verified by a new RecipeDetail page test asserting an unmatched row survives a save that only tweaked a matched row — full suite 29/29 green. Flagging for review because the live /recipe-detail round-trip can't be screenshotted headlessly (data-less QA test account, empty /nutrition). Please verify on-device, or it rides the next alpha build.
